children: Navitas Semiconductor reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $13.99 million, up 38.4% from the prior-year quarter, while its net loss widened to $37.11 million and diluted loss per share was $0.14. Growth was driven primarily by U.S. data-center demand.
¹ Reported as “Net revenues”. ² Reported as “Net loss”. ³ Reported as “Diluted loss per share attributable to common stockholders”.
Nine-month revenue fell 14% as weaker mobile and consumer sales in Asia, particularly China, partly offset growth in U.S. data-center demand.
The Navitas 2.0 restructuring was substantially complete by September 30, refocusing the business on high-power, higher-margin markets.
Navitas acquired Claros on October 6, adding integrated voltage-regulator technology for AI data centers and extending its solutions from the grid to xPU.
Management expects operating losses and negative operating cash flows to continue, with research and development, administrative expenses and capital spending increasing.
